name: Food delivery operators and dark stores

problems.words: App shows items in stock that aren't on the shelf, then we cancel
quick_ideas: Count your top-selling items on the shelf against what the records say once, so you see the size of the gap
Fix bin locations for those items, so pickers find them.

workzap_build.text: Hub stock with shelf locations, stock counts and mismatch alerts, updated on your online listings right when items move.

problems.ask_first: How often is the hub counted?
problems.free_stops: The count routine and sync set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the fastest-moving shelf after the evening rush and note missing lines still showing available, so cancellations can be traced to specific items.
Give one staff member the closing shelf check and one notebook for mismatches, so stock updates stop being missed between picking and replenishment.

problems.words: Pickers pick wrong items and missing-item complaints come every day
quick_ideas: Check a sample of bags before handover, so you see the most common mistake
Pair new pickers with experienced ones for their first shifts.

workzap_build.text: a pick-and-pack screen with scan confirmation and a bag photo before handover.

problems.ask_first: What's the most common picking mistake?
problems.free_stops: The pick-and-pack checks are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Open a handful of completed bags before rider handover and note the exact item mistakes, so you see whether confusion starts in similar packs or labels.
Make one picker responsible for the final bag glance at every handover, so missing items are caught before complaints reach the store.

problems.words: Rider COD cash comes in short or days late
quick_ideas: Settle each rider's COD at the end of every shift, so cash doesn't sit with them
Keep a record of expected cash per rider per shift.

workzap_build.text: COD settlement per rider ID showing expected against handed in, with ageing of unremitted cash.

problems.ask_first: How and to whom do riders hand in cash now?
problems.free_stops: The settlement routine and ageing rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note each cash order total beside the rider handover time, so you see which route periods create late or short returns.
Keep one notebook at dispatch for cash order totals and handover signatures, so COD returns are checked at the same place every shift.

problems.words: Orders breach the delivery promise at peak hours
quick_ideas: Note late orders by hour and zone for a week, so you see where it happens
Plan more riders for the worst hour.

workzap_build.text: a daily view of delivery times by hub, zone and hour set against the promised time.

problems.ask_first: When do late deliveries happen most?
problems.free_stops: The rider and slot planning approach stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note order ready time and rider departure time during the evening peak, so you can see whether delay starts in picking or dispatch.
Give one dispatcher the peak-hour handover board and update time, so waiting orders are assigned in the order they are actually ready.

problems.words: Riders don't log in for the evening rush, and shifts are made on WhatsApp the night before
quick_ideas: Publish next week's rider shifts on a fixed day, so riders plan ahead
Ask each rider to confirm, so gaps show early.

workzap_build.text: a rider shift planner by hub and hour with confirmations and no-show reports.

problems.ask_first: Are riders employed, freelance or through an agency?
problems.free_stops: The shift planning rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the planned evening roster with who actually logs in across the week, so the no-show pattern is clear before the next rush.
Give one person the weekly rider roster and one chat thread for confirmations, so evening coverage stops changing in scattered messages.

problems.words: Fresh produce and dairy expire on the shelf
quick_ideas: Check expiry dates on fresh and chilled items daily, so they're moved before they expire
Order fresh items in smaller amounts more often.

workzap_build.text: an expiry tracker by batch and shelf with prompts to mark down or remove.

problems.free_stops: The expiry rules per category stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the fresh and chilled shelves each morning and note items nearest expiry by section, so wastage is linked to specific display areas.
Give one staff member the daily short-date check and one shelf note for removals, so older stock gets attention before new stock is placed.

problems.words: Riders' fuel and bike maintenance claims are inflated
quick_ideas: Compare a week of fuel claims with trips done, so you see if there's a real gap
Require approval for repair claims before work is done.

workzap_build.text: a bike maintenance and fuel claim log with approvals.

problems.free_stops: The claim rules and approvals are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, compare each rider's fuel and repair claims with the routes they actually covered, so inflated claims stand out by rider and route.
Make one dispatcher note any bike issue when a rider returns, so later repair claims can be checked against the shift handover.

problems.words: Customers order once with a promo code and never return
quick_ideas: Look at which first orders led to a second, so you see what brings people back
Ask a few one-time customers why they didn't return.

workzap_build.text: a customer list with order history and repeat offers for customers who opted in.

problems.ask_first: How do you spot promo abuse today?
problems.free_stops: The repeat-order plan stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one-time orders by basket type and delivery experience notes, so you can see which early orders fail to earn a second purchase.
Give one person the weekly review of first-order complaints in one notebook, so repeat-loss reasons are gathered in one place.

problems.words: Every hub's numbers come from a different spreadsheet
quick_ideas: Ask every hub for the same few numbers each day, so they can be compared
Pick the one number you'll check each morning.

workzap_build.text: a daily hub comparison on WhatsApp with orders, late deliveries, stock issues and COD outstanding.

problems.ask_first: How many hubs do you run?
problems.free_stops: What goes into the daily read is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Lay out yesterday's hub figures side by side on one page, so missing numbers and mismatched definitions show up immediately.
Give one person the morning collection of hub numbers in one notebook, so every location reports into the same place each day.

never_say: Anything about labour or gig-worker law, rider visas, insurance, vehicle licensing or traffic rules.
Covert tracking of riders' personal phones or tracking outside work.
Regulatory advice on pharmacy or age-restricted items.
Help hiding rider cash shortages, charging riders unlawfully or manipulating reported delivery times.
That delivery times or costs will improve by a set amount.

sample_reply.person: We run 4 dark stores in Lahore. Biggest headache is COD cash from riders, some hold it for days. Need a fix.
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be fixed, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, settle each rider's COD at the end of every shift, so cash doesn't sit with them.
Second, keep a record of expected cash per rider per shift, so any gap is clear.
To make it stick, Workzap could build: with a COD settlement tool per rider ID showing expected against handed in at every hub and how long any cash has been outstanding.

Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
